title: FedEx Expands Asia–U.S. Shipping Capacity Ahead of Peak Season
summary: Continued investment strengthens connectivity to Thailand’s largest export market and supports growing demand across technology, manufacturing, and premium e-commerce
body_markdown:
BANGKOK, Thailand, November 9, 2026 – Federal Express Corporation, one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, has expanded its trans-Pacific network with an additional 567,000 kilograms (1.25 million pounds) of weekly capacity between Asia Pacific, including Thailand, and the United States. The new five-times-weekly Boeing 777F service is expected to help businesses across advanced industrial manufacturing, semiconductor production, AI infrastructure, and premium e-commerce access additional capacity to support rising customer demand during one of the busiest trading periods of the year.


The additional capacity strengthens connectivity to the United States, Thailand’s largest single-country export market in 2025, and a key destination for electronics, computer equipment, telecommunications products, and other high-value manufactured goods[\[1\]](https://tradingeconomics.com/thailand/exports/united-states)


. As Thai businesses work to meet customer delivery commitments and maintain service levels during a period of heightened shipping activity, the enhanced service provides additional support for time-sensitive shipments moving across the Pacific.


The new service operates through three routing variationsconnecting our Asia Pacific hub in Guangzhou and sub-regional hubs in Shanghai, China; Osaka, Japan; and our gateway Clark, Philippines, via Anchorage, Alaska, to the FedEx World hub in Memphis, Tennessee. Businesses in Thailand will access the additional U.S.-bound capacity via Clark. This expanded network provides customers flexibility, capacity, and connectivity to reach U.S. customers and respond quickly to changing customer demands.


The enhanced network also introduces a new five-times-weekly connection for Asia Pacific customers to Dallas–Fort Worth via Anchorage, providing an additional gateway to one of the United States’ leading technology and data center markets.


Thailand’s technology-related trade has been expanding. According to SCB Economic Intelligence Center (SCB EIC), Thai electronics exports grew 67.8% year on year in July 2026, while imports of electrical and electronic appliances and components increased 138.4%, reflecting activity across technology-related supply chains[\[2\]](https://www.scbeic.com/th/detail/product/trade-270826?utm_source=Twitter&utm_medium=Twitter)


.


The additional capacity comes as businesses navigate growing trans-Pacific trade volumes and increasingly interconnected supply chains. According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA) Air Cargo Market Analysis, the Asia–North America corridor recorded 9% year-on-year growth in July 2026, making it the fastest-growing major air cargo trade lane globally \[3\]


.


“Global supply chains are becoming increasingly interconnected, particularly across advanced manufacturing, AI-related industries, and premium e-commerce,” said Salil Chari, president, Asia Pacific, FedEx. “The addition of this capacity comes at a critical time as customers prepare for increased shipping volumes ahead of the year-end peak season. Businesses need reliable access to capacity, speed and global connectivity to serve customers and keep supply chains moving. These additional flights strengthen links between Asia Pacific and key U.S. markets, including Dallas–Fort Worth, while supporting semiconductor, technology and AI-related industries.”


“For exporters, every shipment represents a commitment to a customer. Whether fulfilling holiday orders, supporting production schedules, or replenishing inventory, businesses need confidence that they can meet expectations when it matters most,” said Sasathorn Phaspinyo, managing director, FedEx Thailand. “Our continued investments in Thailand and across our global network reflect our commitment to supporting customers as they serve their own customers and manage international shipping needs.”


The service builds on a series of network enhancements introduced across Asia Pacific over the past year, including expanded flight connectivity from Bangkok, Penang and Sydney to the Guangzhou hub. Together, these investments help customers access international markets more efficiently, strengthen supply chain resilience and capitalize on emerging growth opportunities.
